articleTitle: Bioinspired Clustering in UWSNs Using Monarch Butterfly Optimization Compared with Ant Colony Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The Monarch Butterfly Optimization (MBO) algorithm for clustering in Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (UWSNs) is investigated and compared to the performance of the Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm in this paper. As is evident from the outcomes depicted in the above graphs MBO consumes an average of 31% less energy than the ACO while lasting longer in the network. 7J or make a network get 790 round life cycle while ACO did 34. 5J and 730 rounds. The results indicate that MBO is more advantageous to cluster in the UWSNs making it a viable solution to boost up the network productivity and the overall energy utilization efficiency.

articleTitle: 5G Advanced: A Step Towards 6G
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This article explores the features and proximity of 5G advanced (well known as 5.5G) to 6G cellular communication system, emphasizing its speed, connectivity, and intelligence. Expected benefits of 5.5G include an enhanced user experience, industrial revolution, and support for the Internet of Things (IoT). The motivation behind 5.5G arises from addressing 5G limitations, accommodating IoT growth, enabling real-time applications, providing personalized experiences, and driving economic growth. Anticipated applications span from enhanced mobile broadband to ultra-reliable low latency communication and IoT-based massive machine-type communication, extending to personalized experiences, next-gen gaming, connected healthcare, and advanced education. Despite being in development, 5.5G holds immense significance for bridging the physical and digital world, fostering innovation, and unlocking the potential of the digital age.

articleTitle: Extensive Review of Epileptic Seizure Detection Techniques: Performance, Achievements, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Epilepsy is a neurological illness that affects the brain on a chronic and crucial basis. It is characterized by recurring seizures. These seizures involve phases of synchronous, abnormal neural activity, lasting from a few seconds to several minutes. Epileptic seizures manifest as transient episodes of involuntary body movements, often accompanied by a loss of consciousness. Although individual patients experience seizures infrequently, the impacts on physical health, social interactions, and emotional well-being are substantial, necessitating careful diagnosis and treatment.This review provides a thorough examination of the many machine learning methods employed for epilepsy detection, drawing insights from numerous research studies. It evaluates the features considered in each study and offers a thorough comparison of their performance metrics. Additionally, the survey investigates the highest performance levels achieved, the datasets utilized, and the simulation tools applied in the research. The review concludes by identifying existing research gaps and challenges, providing valuable insights for future advancements within the domain of epileptic seizure detection.

articleTitle: Heating and Cooling Jacket for Military for Optimal Comfort
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Military personnel operating in extreme environments experience significant thermal stress, impacting comfort and performance. This study presents a novel design for a temperature-controlled jacket aimed at enhancing soldier performance. The jacket utilizes a Peltier module for efficient heating and cooling, with heat sink cooler maximizing heat dissipation. A water pump ensures circulation of temperature-controlled water throughout the garment, maintaining optimal body temperature for the wearer. A 12V relay controls the system activation. This design has the potential to significantly improve soldier comfort and performance in harsh environments.

articleTitle: Classification of Cognitive Stress with StressGAN-GP
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative Deep Learning (DL) architecture for classifying cognitive stress using a novel hybrid model, StressGAN-GP. The increasing prevalence of stress-related disorders in modern society necessitates accurate and efficient methods for stress detection and classification. This study aims to improve the model's generalization to various stress-inducing events by utilizing the capabilities of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to synthesize stress-related patterns from limited labelled data. The suggested StressGAN-GP system blends the Gradient Penalty's interpretability with GANs' prowess in producing realistic stress characteristics. The proposed StressGAN-GP framework combines the strengths of GANs in generating realistic stress features with the interpretability of Gradient Penalty. The GAN component generates synthetic stress patterns, enriching the training dataset, while the GP component provides a probabilistic framework for stress classification, offering insights into model uncertainty. Test findings on an extensive dataset show that StressGAN-GP outperforms conventional classification models in terms of performance. The model accurately distinguishes between stressed and non-stressed individuals bearing an accuracy of 98.78%, showcasing its potential for real-world stress monitoring and intervention applications. This research contributes to advancing the field of affective computing and lays the foundation for more robust and interpretable models in the realm of cognitive stress classification.

articleTitle: BERT-based Models for Predicting Protein-Protein Interaction Sites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: In this work, a BERT-based model is proposed for predicting potential PPI sites with the aid of its remarkable contextual understanding feat. Thus, the model was adjusted to a set of positive PPI sites, containing 268 sites in total with the accuracy of 0. 89, precision of 0. 88, recall of 0. IL is 0. 78, accuracy of 0. 85, precision of 0. 83, and F1-score of 0. tested on face images achieving a performance of 87% which is higher than that of conventional models such as CNNs and SVMs. Only hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation have been used to make sure that the model is not overfitting to the data and it can produce reasonable results on unseen data as well. The results of this study also indicate that BERT-based models can be effectively utilized in the bioinformatics field, opening up myriad possibilities for future utilization of computational approaches in the prediction of PPIs.

articleTitle: Ant Lion Optimizer for Robust UWSNs Communication Protocols
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: In this research study, the authors examine the use of the Ant Lion Optimizer (ALO) in building reliable communication models for the Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (UWSNs). Citing some of the challenges unique to the UWSNs include high latencies, low bandwidth and constrained power. The ALO-based protocol proposed for implementation will support efficient selection of routing paths, utilization of energy resources and overall, network scalability, and robustness. Simulation results revealed that the ALO-based protocol has better performance compared to other methods by at least 15% in terms of routing energy, packet delivery, network lifetime, and latency. This research benefits the further advancement of UWSNs by suggesting the improvement of present technologies, and may be used in a number of underwater operations.

articleTitle: Transforming Crime Scene Investigations Through the Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Digital Forensics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The incorporation of artificial intelligence into digital forensics enlarges CSI by increasing the efficacy, precision, execution throughput, and inclusion in trial of physical evidence. Key findings from this study are that the use of AI in these technologies can reduce the required time on key forensic tasks by up to 93%, with the metadata extraction time going down from 10hrs to 2hrs. Here the ameliorations were demonstrable- facial recognition surged from 70pc to 88pc and objects detection in videos also boosted from 65pc to 90pc. These automation features reduced the manual complexity to a great extent It gave 80% reduction in aspect of feature extraction and 88% reduction in report generation. Also, it was observed that the legal admissibility of AI-generated evidence have been enhanced and that, there was a rise in statistics shows that the predictive analytics admissibility, which was at 70%, had risen to 85% on average. These results clearly indicate the applicability of Artificial Intelligence technology in the process of overhaul for digital forensic science and in the overall improvement of investigative performance.

articleTitle: Automated Design of CMOS-DACML Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This paper presents a new method for designing a differential amplifier using CMOS technology, incorporating a current mirror load (CMOS-DACML). To tackle the intricate optimization challenges presented by this nonlinear and multidimensional problem, the study utilizes a combined optimization strategy called fitness-based adaptive differential evolution with particle swarm optimization (ADEPSO). Through this hybrid approach, the design achieves substantial enhancements across critical performance metrics. Specifically, it achieves a notable reduction in power dissipation, lowering it to 520.60 µW. Moreover, the amplifier demonstrates a higher gain of 44.70 dB, significantly reduced output capacitance of 4.20 pF, and an enhanced cutoff frequency reaching 103.60 kHz. These outcomes highlight the effectiveness of ADEPSO in tackling the intricate challenges associated with differential amplifier design, especially in the context of CMOS-DACML. By optimizing these parameters simultaneously, the approach not only improves performance metrics but also underscores its potential for future applications in integrated circuit design and optimization.

articleTitle: Intelligent Time Management Recommendations Using Bayesian Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This paper focuses on the improvement of the intelligent time management system which employ Bayesian optimization for suggesting time management plans for each particular person. In this sense, through historical data of input-output patterns and users’ preferences, the system aims at increasing productivity and user satisfaction. In the study, Gaussian Processes are used as the surrogate model in the Bayesian optimization so that the required evaluations by the algorithm to realize optimal scheduling methodologies are kept to a minimum. Implementation is done as a web application where users submit their tasks and get the recommended schedule instantly. Indicators like, the degree of task accomplishment, time, and scheduling compliance, and probably the users’ satisfaction suggest that system helped enhance time management results. Lack of feedback from the users is removed through questionnaire that reveals the simplicity of the system and the quality of its recommended times, thereby supporting the idea of Bayesian optimization as a game changer in the management of time. This research significance points to the need for maintaining efficient and individualized approaches to time management strategies and agrees with others’ findings, which suggest that this is an area ample fiction research needs to acknowledge and pursue.

articleTitle: Comparing the Absorption Characteristics of Different Fractal Shapes as Unit Cells for THz Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: In this paper, a comparison of the absorption characteristics of three fractal shaped unit cells augmented with graphene in THz frequency range is presented. The unit cells chosen for this study are the Haferman carpet, Sierpinski carpet, and a variant of the Sierpinski gasket. The proposed metasurface unit cell consists of monolayer graphene and bottom layer gold insulated by Alumina (Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>). Among the 3 different fractal shapes, the Sierpinski gasket gives the widest absorption bandwidth of 1.32 THz above 80% absorption rate for a graphene chemical potential 1.0 eV. The proposed absorber is characterized by invoking parametric studies of incident angles. The suggested absorber can be utilized for THz imaging as well as signal absorption to prevent scattering in undesired directions.

articleTitle: Mouse Cursor Control Using Dynamic Hand Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Hand gestures are the most common way of interaction among humans in the physical world. Gestures are used in everyday life to interact with objects around us. Hand gesture is becoming the most comfortable alternative technique to replace the conventional mouse. Herein, we report the development of a dynamic hand gesture user interface that tracks and recognizes in real time based on color segmentation and recognition. Operation such as file dragging, right and left clicks and scrolling up and down has been studied. The colors are calibrated in order to make sure that no other similar shades of color from the background interfere during the process.

articleTitle: Metamaterials:The future matter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Metamaterials are engineered materials, which are generally not found in nature i.e. their behaviors are very much different from general laws of physics. Their one or more property is modified so that they retaliate in a desired manner. Most of the human progress is constrained by material limits. The main aim is to improve the basic design and capability of materials to conduct tasks which are usually impossible to achieve with normal materials, to go beyond the limits of general material characteristics. The results are farfetched and beyond existing imagination. Various laws of optics, acoustics, thermodynamics and electromagnetics are redefined due to evolution of these materials. Meta materials interact with these physical phenomenon to do wonders like super lenses, cloaking, superconductivity of power in space etc

articleTitle: Interconnection of SDN node with conventional network using an ONOS controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: For future network design, different architectures worldwide have been proposed; among them, one of the finest network designs is Software-Defined Networking (SDN), which separates the network data and control layers and enables the network with more agility, programmability, and flexibility. However, because of economic and technical challenges, directly upgrading the whole network to SDN is challenging for many organizations, and the optimal solution is to upgrade conventional network devices incrementally to SDN nodes, which is the Hybrid SDN. In a hybrid SDN environment, SDN nodes interconnect with the traditional legacy network, which takes advantage of both network designs. In this paper, we studied the integration of SDN with conventional legacy networks. We explore how to peer and integrate SDN nodes with conventional networks using the SDN-IP application located on the top of the application layer of the ONOS controller. Through different experiments on both networks, IP-IP and IP-SDN, we found that compared to IP-IP networks, IP-SDN improves the overall network performance and provides more outstanding performance in maximization of throughput and minimization of delay.

articleTitle: VDTA and CDTA based Grounded Flux Controlled Meminductor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This work presents a novel method for designing a meminductor emulator with the goal of lowering circuit complexity. One VDTA (Voltage differencing transconductance amplifier), one CDTA (current differencing transconductance amplifier) two capacitors, make up the design that is being given. It has a maximum working frequency of 1MHz and conducted in incremental and decremental mode between -55°C and 125°C. To investigate several facets of the behavior of the circuit, theoretical analyses are done. Furthermore, pinched hysteresis loop (PHL) in 180nm TSMC technology has been analyzed for many parameters at varying applied frequencies. Moreover, Monte Carlo Analysis is performed to assess the suggested circuit's efficiency for variations in various parameters falling within a reasonable range. Lastly, a nonvolatility test is used to determine the circuit's retention property.

articleTitle: Sustainable Solar Powered Bluetooth Enabled Smart Home Automation System Using Internet-of-Things
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: People have always strived hard since long in order to develop a technology that eases their workload. The Home automation technology is a crucial example of such an innovation that humans have developed in order to simplify their tasks. It deals with creating a network between all the devices in the home, from LED lights and fans to even doors and more. Automating these tasks ensure that they happen simultaneously one after the other. In addition to that when we want to seek more control of things, the concept of Internet of Things come into play. IoT will involve integrating these automated systems with a connectivity layer and then transmitting the data across various devices and interfaces. In this paper, Bluetooth is used for the connectivity purpose. Wireless connectivity will allow the user to remotely access all the devices, which opens numerous possibilities. Furthermore, this paper promotes energy conservation as the system will automatically adjust the device operations according to the external environmental conditions. Moreover, the entire system is solar powered adding a sustainable and eco-friendly touch to the paper.

articleTitle: Hybrid Bioinspired Algorithms for UWSNs: Combining Genetic Algorithm and PSO
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This work proposes a GA-PSO Metaheuristic Algorithm to improve the throughputs and network efficiency of the UWSNs based on using a new technology of WSNs which is Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks. In response to the difficulties of underwater communication, a hybrid GA-PSO algorithm is designed to fit the needs, where GA excels in search capabilities, and PSO accomplishes optimization adjustments. The realistic network model was developed using realistic network topology with MATLAB NS-3 and the integrated GA-PSO hybrid approach was found to significantly enhance the throughput energy efficiency and overall network lifetime as compared to the other routing protocols GA & PSO individually. Based on these findings, it could therefore be concluded that the proposed hybrid bioinspired algorithms can potentially help enhance the efficiency and dependability of UWSNs significantly.

articleTitle: Applying ML Models for Heart Disease Prediction: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The human body is always susceptible to disease. Heart-related issues are a major concern among them, leading to more annual fatalities than all other diseases combined. It includes various conditions that impact the heart arrhythmias, among others. Alarmingly, heart disease is increasingly prevalent among younger generations, particularly among youth. Research indicates that factors such as chronic stress, smoking, and unhealthy lifestyles contribute to this trend. Given the rising incidence of heart disease, there is a pressing need for advanced algorithms and methodologies for predicting its occurrence. This study aims to determine whether an individual is currently suffering from or is at risk of developing heart disease. Hospitals can leverage automated diagnostic tools that utilize computations for data science and data mining techniques for accurate predictions. This research paper examines the application of supervised ML methods, specifically highlighting the Decision Trees (DT) model, alongside two other models: the Random Forest (RF) model and the LR model. The dataset that was utilized in this investigation came from Kaggle. The Decision Tree and Logistic Regression algorithms demonstrated notable accuracy rates of 88% and 84%, respectively. In contrast, the Random Forest model outperformed the others, achieving an accuracy of 92.74%, almost 93%.

articleTitle: Biotic Stress and Severity Classification of Pear Leaves Disease with Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Leaf disease frequently arises as pears plants mature. With a particular emphasis on categorizing the pear leaf disease, the proposed research work suggests the implementation of the CNN architecture that we use in this study to create this disease identification and classification method comprised of ResNet50, InceptionV3, VGG16, and VGG19. These neural networks have been pre-trained on the ImageNet dataset. The ensemble methodology that we describe produces final predictions for the test samples based on the recall, precision, accuracy, and f1-score scores of four standard evaluation metrics. Even though there is an increase in the amount of accuracy when the models are ensembled, the remarkable combination is InceptionV3 with VGG16 with an accuracy of 77.25%, precision of 79.34%, recall of 77.25% and F1 score of 76.50% and with the severity classification as accuracy 45.29%, precision 46.88%, recall 45.29% and F1 score 45.50% respectively.

articleTitle: Seagull Optimization Algorithm for Underwater Sensor Network Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This paper presents a new technique to a position sensor in UWSNs with the recognition of the Seagull Optimization Algorithm. UWSNs are particularly useful for applications in environmental monitoring and military monitoring, but accurate sensor localization is difficult due to the signal loss in underwater environments and in the presence of external factors. Based on the Motivation Model, the SOA, motivated by the seagulls’ distributed foraging behavior, is a possible solution to the dilemma by striking a midway between exploration and exploitation. The synthesis of exact methodology is outlined here along with the creation of synthetic dataset and a proof of concept MATLAB code for the evaluation of the proposed SOA-based localization algorithm. A performance evaluation, which involved the use of computational simulations on a wide variety of antennas, clearly shows that the SOA achieves a higher localization accuracy in much shorter time, while consuming less power compared to other methods such as PSO, GA, or hybrid methods. The stability is one more strongest side of proposed algorithm which has been confirmed by robustness analysis, so it can be effectively used in dynamic underwater environment. The current research is not only useful in showing how the SOA can be used for the UWSN localization in specific domains, but also valuable to the development of the new UWSN localization method that is efficient and accurate, for the further expansion of the UWSN in the vital marine sphere.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Sequencing Data Compression and Storage Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: They produce huge amount of data which require efficient compression and management mechanisms hence the need to adopt Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS). In this paper, the performance of different compression algorithms and their implementation with local and cloud-based storage systems are assessed and compared using the lossless and lossy storage efficiency analysis. This study reveals that reference-based compression shows the highest compression ratio on the whole with lossy methods having shorter processing time ahead of other methods. A comparison of the costs shows the feasibility of local and cloud storage options to bear substantial costs. The study further supports that sophisticated algorithms as well as universally recognized formats are crucial for organizing NGS data Stream.

articleTitle: 2 x 2 Microstrip Patch Antenna Array for Improving the Power Conversion Efficiency of RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: RF energy harvesting harvests free and wasted energy from the surroundings and converts it into useful DC power. A microstrip patch antenna is widely used in RF energy harvesting because it provides high gain, large bandwidth, good impedance, polarization, and resonant frequency. In this paper, a design and analysis of a microstrip patch antenna array for RF energy harvesting is done. The antenna used is a 2 x 2 microstrip patch antenna array which is simulated using Advanced Design System 2022. Patch microstrip antennas are initially designed as single patches, and to create more complex array configurations. In this article, we will explore the transformation of a single patch into a 2 x 1 and a 2 x 2 patch microstrip array antenna. A single-patch microstrip antenna simulation reveals impressive performance metrics. When tested, the antenna demonstrates a directivity of 6.5 dBi, a gain of 3.5 dBi, and an efficiency of 52.34% at a frequency of 2.4 GHz.. When simulated, the 2 x 1 patch shows a directivity of 8.36 dBi, a gain of 5.77 dBi, and an efficiency of 55.18% at a frequency of 2.4 GHz. When a 2 x 2 patch is simulated shows a directivity of 11.27 dBi, gain of 8.72 dBi, and efficiency of 55.56% at the same frequency. Gain, directivity, and efficiency improvement are obtained in a 2 x 2 patch microstrip antenna. If such an antenna is used for RF energy harvesting higher power conversion efficiency of around 90% is achieved.

articleTitle: Suppression of Mutual coupling and cross-polarization between Closely Spaced Microstrip MIMO Antennas by using a planar frequency-selective surface structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This research work presents a novel configuration of frequency-selective structure (FSS) structures aimed at minimizing mutual coupling between the radiating elements whose side by side distance is 0.03λ (1.975mm) where λ is the wavelength in the dielectric medium. The main issue with close spacing MIMO antennas is their high mutual coupling (MC), which negatively impacts their overall performance, leading to degradation in antenna performance. To tackle this challenge, a solution is proposed, inserting a frequency-selective surface (FSS) structure between the antennas, serving as a decoupling mechanism. Periodic structures like FSS can effectively decrease mutual coupling by suppressing the propagation of surface waves within a specific range of frequency. Using the IE3D EM simulator, the antenna parameters were simulated, achieving a remarkable suppression of 14dB in mutual coupling at the resonating frequency of 4.85GHz. The antenna has proven to be suitable for many applications in the area of wireless communication, WLAN (Wireless Local Area Network), and satellite communication systems.

articleTitle: Scalable Fire Classification with MobileNetV2-Driven Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Public safety and the avoidance of extensive damage depend on the prompt and precise identification of fire. The creation of effective and trustworthy fire classification systems is required due to the rising frequency and intensity of wildfires throughout the world. Climate change is making wildfires a more serious concern, therefore finding creative solutions that support the sustainable development goals is imperative. In order to achieve high accuracy and efficiency, this article provide a fire classification model that uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with MobileNetV2 architecture. Taking use of MobileNetV2's lightweight design and depth wise separable convolutions, our model is optimized for real-time applications with limited computational resources, like those present in mobile and embedded devices. The proposed model was trained and assessed using a wide range of datasets that included both fire and non-fire photos. The suggested model successfully distinguished between fire and non-fire events, as evidenced by its remarkable 98% classification accuracy. The model's strong feature extraction capabilities and good cross-environment and cross-condition generalization led to this high accuracy. In addition, the model is refined for low-latency inference, which qualifies it for use in real-world scenarios where prompt and accurate fire detection is critical. The potential of the MobileNetV2-based CNN as a workable solution for real-time fire detection in safety-critical applications is highlighted by the combination of high precision and computational economy.

articleTitle: Enhancing 5G Network Throughput Using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: In this research, RL is proposed as a solution towards achieving the dynamic optimization of 5G network throughput hindered by the complexity of Intersystems environments. To this extent, the optimization problem is formulated and modeled within the framework of Markov Decision Process and the study resorts to techniques from Deep Reinforcement Learning leading to the design of adaptive algorithms that optimise various network parameters in real-time. It uses simulated raw 5G network data and other data open for public usage for training it and the application itself is coded in Python programming language with TensorFlow for implementing different algorithms. As for the performance, it could be seen that the RL-optimized approach is superior to traditional methods and leads to better system performance in terms of throughput, latency, energy efficiency and user satisfaction in a number of scenarios. The study identifies the possibility to apply RL to enable the learning capability of 5G networks in supporting new services and optimizing the network performance. This research finding can be beneficial for the advancement of 5G wireless communication technology by demonstrating the versatility and advantages of utilizing RL in the network.

articleTitle: Optimizing White Blood Cell Classification with ResNet50 Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: In medical diagnostics, the categorization of white blood cells (WBCs) is a crucial activity necessary for diagnosing and surveilling many health issues such as immunological diseases, infections, and hematologic malignancies. This paper investigates automatic WBC categorization using deep learning methods, namely the ResNet50 model. ResNet50 is a 50-layer residual network well-known for its deep architecture and residual learning capabilities, enabling it to learn complex patterns and characteristics. The ResNet50 model has been fine-tuned to differentiate between neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils, monocytes, and lymphocytes, among other WBC types. To improve generality and resilience, our method included careful model training, augmentation, and data preprocessing. Standard measures including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score were used to assess the model's performance, which showed that it was effective in obtaining high classification accuracy and reliability. The findings show that WBC classification accuracy and efficiency are greatly increased by the ResNet50 model, which may have advantages for clinical practice. The approach facilitates faster and more precise diagnosis by pathologists by automating the categorization process. This article uses the ResNet50 model, which has a 95% accuracy rate in balanced precision, recall, and f1-scores for categorizing white blood cells.

articleTitle: Enhancing Scalability and Performance in IoT Networks through Off-Chain Data Processing and Blockchain Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of IoT devices has led to an exponential increase in data generation, posing significant challenges in terms of data security, scalability, and performance. This paper proposes an innovative approach to address these challenges by integrating off-chain data aggregation with blockchain technology. Leveraging MongoDB for off-chain storage and Hyperledger Fabric for ensuring data integrity, our approach enhances the scalability and performance of IoT networks. We present a detailed system architecture, implementation details, and performance evaluation to demonstrate the effectiveness of our solution. The results indicate that the proposed method significantly improves data management capabilities, offering a scalable and secure solution for IoT networks.

articleTitle: Jellyfish Search Algorithm for UWSNs Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The results of this research measures the efficacy of JSA in managing energy resources of UWSNs. Thus, it has been observed that JSA has better performance than the LEACH algorithm with to some extent since the energy used by cluster heads by JSA is approximately 27. 8J and a network lifespan of 810 rounds, whereas LEACH’s protocol only succeeds in 31 rounds. 5J and 750 rounds. This demonstrates that JSA can also achieve better clustering with less electrical power for the clusters to handle and for the cluster heads consuming 16J of energy. Based on the outcomes presented in this paper, we can conclude that JSA is a beneficial approach for increasing the energy efficiency and network durability in the UWSNs.

articleTitle: Judging the Psychological Impact of News Articles on Rehab Patients: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Sentiment detection and analysis from review comments of products, blogs and other social media communication is a common practice. Lot of research work have been proposed and established in the domain. While the above may prove to be effective for sales and marketing challenges but the same effort for the sentiment analysis of news articles is scarce. But surprisingly, this can definitely establish as a potentially efficient instrument for medical domain judging the suitability of a news article for individuals with disturbed health condition like depression, heart diseases or mental retardation having risk of committing suicides. To address the same, this article presents a novel approach harnessing the potential of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) to detect the sentiment of a news article so as to measure its impact on the individual readers. The proposed work uses various supervised ML algorithms such as SVM, Naïve Bayes’, Logistic Regression, Random Forest and Ensemble Method for assessing the inherent sentiment of news articles. Additionally, DL based Transformer model specifically BERT has also been employed to enhance the performance. Obtained results with various performance metrics clearly depict our model’s excellent performance.

articleTitle: Discovering Roads from High-Resolution Satellite Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Urban roads are prone to issues including insufficient road construction, poor topological connection, and low accuracy in satellite images because of the surrounding ground characteristics, such as building and tree shadows. It is often difficult to accurately separate the road from its background due to the intricate arrangement of the buildings and the sensor's acquisition geometry. These issues will also exist for mountain roads, such as hill shadow or vegetation occlusion. Significant progress has been made in recent years in creating advanced algorithms that can accurately and automatically identify and extract roadways from satellite photos. This study suggests integrating the optimal feature selection and Decision Tree Method with Hierarchical Framework and Ensemble Learning (HFEL). Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) of three distinct varieties, including AlexNet, LeNet-5, and ResNet are utilised by the HFEL.

articleTitle: Design of Antenna Array of 2x1 Configuration for Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This research paper meticulously examines the sophisticated design and rigorous evaluation of a 2x1 antenna array, intricately customized for advanced microwave imaging applications. The inquiry prioritizes the enhancement of pivotal performance metrics, such as return loss, gain, bandwidth, and radiation pattern. The analysis incorporates FR-4 substrate material, notable for its lossy characteristics and a dielectric constant of 4.4, thereby ensuring a profound alignment with pragmatic real-world scenarios. Extensive electromagnetic simulations were conducted, fine-tuning the antenna array design to achieve a remarkable return loss of -33.68 dB and a bandwidth of 2.18 GHz. Additionally, the array exhibited a gain of 5.28 dB, demonstrating its applicability in microwave imaging scenarios. To validate the simulation results, 2x1 antenna array were fabricated and tested. These measurements aligned with the simulation data, confirming a return loss of - 32.27 dB, an extended bandwidth of 2.53 GHz, and gain of 2.53 dB. The antenna array retained its omnidirectional radiation pattern, ensuring a consistent signal. The combined use of simulation and experimental validation underscores the practical feasibility and reliability of antenna array, paving the way for advanced microwave imaging systems with improved resolution and accuracy.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Models for Early Heart Disease Prediction: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: One of the many major health issues, heart disease is one that primarily impacts the cardiovascular system, encompassing the heart and its associated organs. Individuals who smoke, suffer from high blood pressure, have elevated cholesterol levels, maintain poor dietary habits, lack physical activity, or are overweight or obese face an increased risk of developing heart disease. The most frequently diagnosed cardiovascular condition is coronary artery disease (CAD), while other types include congestive heart failure, arrhythmias, and congenital heart defects. This condition is often referred to as cardiovascular disease. Prompt and accurate diagnosis is essential for saving lives and preventing additional complications. Recent advancements in machine learning diagnostic techniques have demonstrated enhanced reliability and effectiveness in detecting heart disease. In this study, we applied three machine learning models: K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naïve Bayes (NB) and Decision Tree, to assess their performance in predicting heart disease using the UCI dataset. The algorithms take into account various factors such as age, gender, resting blood pressure, cholesterol levels, blood sugar levels, and ECG results. The results reveal that the KNN model achieves an accuracy of 87%, the SVM model attains an accuracy of 87%, NB 79% and the Decision Tree model surpasses the others with an impressive accuracy of 96%.

articleTitle: Efficient Information Digest: Exploring AI- Driven PDF Summarization through Streamlit, Open API, and LangChain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: With a focus on combining API functions with LangChain, this initiative aims to develop an AI-driven web application for summarising PDFs using Streamlit. Given the growing growth of PDF consumption, there is a strong demand for a cost-effective, efficient, and user-friendly user interface that can help academics and students manage large data sets.The software's primary purpose is to collect and analyse data effectively by combining context-aware LangChain inquiry and answer technology with API integration. This program, which emphasises speed, cost-effectiveness, and convenience of use, aims to address the growing demand for efficient PDF summarisation. The primary goal is to create a dynamic web application that can adapt to the changing needs of users in the demanding disciplines of academia and research.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Cyber Security System Approach using Machine Learning Techniques on KDD-99 Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Internet is used in everywhere in our day-to-day life & it led to rise in cyberattacks. As people are rely on digital platform, cybercriminals get opportunities to explore their vulnerabilities & grow cybercrime so there is need to developed robust cyber security system is paramount. This paper covers comprehensive approach to enhanced cybersecurity with the help of machine learning by specially focused on well-known KDD99 dataset. In this paper, introduction section describes significance of cybersecurity, its different types & potential of machine learning to detect & mitigate cyber-attack. In review of literature, Literature related to machine learning using KDD99 dataset by highlighting existing research & methods are given. Paper mainly focused on proposed model using KDD99 dataset & its structure that integrates machine learning classification algorithm & benchmark dataset for intrusion detection is extensively review that also includes overview, types of attack, features & various attack categories like DOS, R2L, U2R & Probing are discussed. For calculating performance of the model, Naïve bayes, DT, RF, SVM, LR and GB classifier is used. Performance of all machine learning classifier is calculated by using accuracy parameter. Amongst them random forest machine learning classifier gives outperforming result over all classifier that showcasing potential of these technique in real world cybersecurity applications. This developed system helps in contributing to safeguard the digital infrastructure.

articleTitle: Leveraging Grey Wolf Optimizer for Reliable Data Transmission in Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This research investigates the application of the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) to enhance reliable data transmission in Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (UWSNs). UWSNs are critical for various applications, including environmental monitoring and underwater exploration, but face challenges such as high propagation delays, limited bandwidth, and energy constraints. The GWO algorithm, inspired by the social hierarchy and hunting behavior of grey wolves, is employed to optimize routing paths, minimize energy consumption, and improve packet delivery ratio. The methodology includes simulating UWSNs with different network configurations using synthetic and real-world datasets, and implementing the GWO algorithm in Python within the NS-3 simulation framework. Comparative analysis with traditional routing protocols, AODV and DSR, demonstrates that the GWO-based routing algorithm significantly reduces energy consumption, increases packet delivery ratio, lowers latency, and extends network lifetime. These results underscore the effectiveness of GWO in enhancing UWSN performance. The study concludes that GWO offers a robust and adaptable solution for reliable data transmission in UWSNs, with potential for further enhancements through hybrid optimization techniques and real-world validations. This research provides a comprehensive understanding of GWO's application in UWSNs, contributing to advancements in underwater communication technologies.

articleTitle: A Brief Review of TOPCon Solar Cell and its Future Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The utilization of poly-Si/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> structures for passivating contacts, commonly referred to as TOPCon (Tunnel Oxide Passivated Contacts), presents a significant opportunity to enhance the efficiency of crystalline silicon solar cells. Laboratory-scale implementations have achieved efficiencies exceeding 26%, while industrial-scale cells have demonstrated efficiencies surpassing 24%. The reported efficiency pertains to a larger wafer that includes metal fingers and bus-bars under full illumination and simulated conditions. This work shows that the device’s actual deployment is severely hampered by recombination losses in the emitter, which span surface, bulk and metal contacts. The historical evolution of such contact structures, which started decades ago, is summarized in this paper together with the state-of-the-art in both laboratory and industry settings to date.

articleTitle: Segmentation of Liver Tumors in CT Scans Using Active Contour Models and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Liver tumor segmentation in CT scans plays a crucial role in cancer diagnosis and treatment planning. This paper proposes a novel methodology that integrates Active Contour Models (ACMs) with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for accurate and efficient segmentation of liver tumors. The approach leverages the feature learning capabilities of deep learning and the precise boundary detection of ACMs to achieve state-of-the-art segmentation results. Evaluation on the LiTS dataset demonstrates superior performance in terms of Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Precision, Recall, and computation time. The proposed methodology offers a promising solution for improving clinical decision-making in liver cancer treatment.

articleTitle: Smart Lock for Enhancing Luggage Security Using Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The escalating incidents of luggage tampering and theft underscore the necessity for robust security measures tailored to modern travelers’ needs. This paper presents a pioneering approach to bolstering luggage security for contemporary travelers through an IoT-based Smart Lock system. With a surge in luggage tampering and theft incidents, conventional security measures have proven inadequate, necessitating innovative solutions. Our Smart Lock system leverages IoT technology to seamlessly integrate with mobile applications, enabling remote locking/unlocking and advanced security functionalities. Key components including NodeMCU, ESP32cam, and vibration sensors work in tandem to ensure robust security. Integration with the Blynk IoT App facilitates intuitive control and alarm setting. Notably, the system incorporates face recognition for intruder detection, further enhancing security measures. Rigorous testing validates the system’s efficacy in detecting intruders and ensuring reliable locking operations.

articleTitle: Circular Shaped Meta-Surface Embedded Monopole Antenna for Ultra-Wideband MIMO Applications with Frequency Notched Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: For applications requiring frequency notching, a revised compact MIMO plan with an integrated UWBA is projected.Two similar monopole antennas powered by two microstrip are used for this configuration. By strategically placing the circular metamaterial elements on the upper side, the gain is increased. The inclusion of a metasurface significantly improves antenna gain compared to conventional designs. Notch frequencies are achieved using L-shaped quarter-wave lines on each antenna lead. This antenna maintains an proper bandwidth of -10 dB throughout the range with a peak frequency of 5.5 GHz to suppress interference from the 5-6 GHz WLAN band. The results obtained from full-wave simulations of the manufactured prototype were experimentally verified for impedance, gain and radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: IoT Enabled Biomedical Smart Waste Bin Monitoring System using YOLO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This research presents an innovative approach to biomedical waste management through the integration of Internet of Things (IoT) technology, computer vision using the YOLO (You Only Look Once) algorithm, and the Raspberry Pi platform. The proposed system aims to enhance the efficiency of waste segregation in biomedical facilities by implementing a smart waste bin equipped with sensors and a camera. The YOLO algorithm is employed for real-time object detection, enabling the system to accurately identify and classify biomedical waste items as they are discarded into the smart waste bin. The Raspberry Pi serves as the central processing unit, orchestrating data collection, analysis, and communication functionalities. The Global Positioning System (GPS) communication is used for sharing the status of the bins using Short Message Service (SMS). Proposed system is a low cost and robust, supports in sustainable environment managing.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Inspired Planar Multi-Band Antenna for Wireless Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to multiband planar monopole antenna design. This technique uses a planar antenna loaded with a subwavelength device called a split ring resonator. The 2.4/5.2GHz WLAN and 3.5/5.5 GHz Wi-MAX bands are both covered by the antenna. It uses the following frequencies to function: 2.34–2.57 GHz, 3.37–4.4 GHz, and 4.62–5.52 GHz. The elevation plane radiation pattern of IEEE 802.11 a/b WLAN frequencies and Wi-Max WLAN frequencies are nearly the same. The highest gain of the split ring resonator loaded antenna is 4 dBi.

articleTitle: Modelling and Design of ANN-based MPPT Controller of SEPIC Converter for SPV Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: An Artificial Neural Network (ANN) based Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm fed Single Ended Primary Inductor Converter (SEPIC) is represented in this paper. For Solar photovoltaic (SPV) applications, as the output power depends on atmospheric conditions, MPPT is required for the successful extraction of maximum power. Steady-state and Small-signal modelling of the converter, in continuous current conduction mode, is analyzed. To improve the stability of the system, an Input Voltage Control (IVC) is developed with proper implementation of a PI-Compensator. Finally, a MATLAB simulation prototype, of 250W 48V, is created, and various voltage and current of the SEPIC converter's properties are verified. Additionally, the enhancement of ANN-MPPT performance is verified by comparison with other conventional MPPT techniques.

articleTitle: Prevention from Road Accidents due to Drunk Driver using IOT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Drinking alcohol is common in social gatherings and parties in some societies. Driving vehicles after drinking may cause road accidents. This paper aims to detect alcoholic drivers and stop them from driving using an IoT system. It is implemented using the Arduino micro-controller. The driver’s alcohol level is measured using an alcohol detector connected to a micro-controller in real-time. When the level of alcohol crosses a permissible limit, the vehicle ignition system will be turned off and the GPS module will capture the present location of the vehicle. Also, the GSM module will automatically send distress messages to police or family members.

articleTitle: Evolutionary Approach-Based Hybrid CNN and SVM for Effective Plant Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Agriculture is one of the prime factors that form the backbone of the economy of India. Also, with its rapidly growing population, the demand for food is increasing manifold. Thus, there arises a dire need to augment agricultural productivity to meet this ever-growing demand. One of the highest challenges that prevents quite ideal crop yields from being acquired is the prevalence of plant diseases, which could be due to many kinds and types of pathogens. For example, bacteria, viruses, fungi, and others are at fault. Thus, the discovery of effective detection systems becomes essential to combat their ill effects. One of the most promising strategies for plant disease identification is using machine learning algorithms. These techniques have proved to be effective in analysis resulting from big data, mainly due to their focus on reaching specific specified results that come out perfectly for identifying plant diseases. Worth noting is that the successful application of machine learning in this setting often requires feature engineering. This is a process that involves the choice and modification of data features likely to enhance the performance of the model. In this paper, we would like to propose a different method of plant disease recognition using convolutional neural networks. The modification of the last layer of the conventional Softmax CNN model opens up an opportunity for enhancing the precision of the approach, done by substituting the usually used Softmax classifier with one based on the k-nearest neighbors algorithm. This will lead us toward better results. The modification uses the ability of this K-NN classifier to work along the labels of the neighboring data points, thus giving better accuracy in decision-making concerning disease detection. Moreover, we have developed an evolutionary algorithm to adjust the parameters of the network for the improvement of accuracy in CNN's performance. This systematic searching technique is one kind of evolutionary technique that seeks to find the appropriate configuration of CNN parameters, which maximizes the model efficiency on plant disease identification tasks.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency in 5G Networks Using Gaussian Mixture Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: In this research, a new approach for improving energy efficiency of the networks in the 5G context is presented: utilizing the Gaussian Mixture Models. The process includes acquiring data in the first step, training the model in the second step, and using the model to make real-time decisions to minimize resources and inefficient energy consumption in the last step. This includes the collection of data on context and complete flow details of the course of traffic passage as well as actions committed by users. The GMM is then trained using the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm for developing the model and reinforcement learning for real-time decision-making on the developed model. In case studies analyzed, there is evidence of the enhancement of energy consumption by 14% on average absolute reduction in energy per traffic unit, by 11% of the average absolute increase in network throughput and by 49% of the mean absolute reduction of latency in comparison with baseline conditions.

articleTitle: An Unified PSO and Fuzzy Satisfaction Framework for Power Flow Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This study introduces a new method for multi-objective optimization (MOO) in electrical power systems, aiming to minimise emission release, power losses and fuel costs concurrently. Diverging from traditional techniques that primarily target cost reduction, the proposed Power Flow Optimization (PFO) framework combines Fuzzy Satisfaction Maximization strategy with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), acknowledging the vagueness in decision-makers’ objectives. By formulating the optimization problem as a fuzzy satisfaction maximization problem, the method aims to find optimal trade-off solutions that balance conflicting objectives. Testing the PFO on a standard IEEE 30-bus system with six generators demonstrates its effectiveness in providing solutions that optimize both actual and imaginary powers while considering fuel cost, emission reduction, and power loss, thereby offering valuable insights for efficient power system operation.

articleTitle: Classification of Cassava Leaf Diseases Using a Pre-trained EfficientNet Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Cassava is one of the staple crops in most tropical and subtropical countries and said to supply the vital food for millions of people. However, the production of this crop is substantially challenged by many leaf diseases, such as the Cassava Mosaic Disease (CMD), the Cassava Brown Streak Disease (CBSD), and the Cassava Bacterial Blight (CBB). In contrast, the traditional methods of disease detection are laborious, time-consuming, and prone to errors due to human intervention in their very nature. This paper works on a pre-trained EfficientNet model for automated cassava leaf disease classification. The work takes advantage of the latest deep-learning techniques to boost the efficiency and accuracy of the process of classifying cassava leaves. As we can see the model gave excellent performance by achieving maximum accuracy at 92.83% with a minimum loss of 0.2019 measured at epoch 16.

articleTitle: Creating a Broadband Matching Network for a Low Noise Amplifier: Design and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The goal of the study in this paper is to design an impedance matching network for a low noise amplifier (LNA). The LNA is typically located behind an antenna or in the back of a simple band-pass sifter behind this aerial, next to the front end of an RF receiver. It is possible to mask the subpar message with a noticeable undesirable signal because of the position within the acceptor pattern. As a result, the LNA both magnifies this message and lessens the specific undesired signal in the magnified message. Using bulk inductor (L) and capacitor (C) parts, a broadband matching network is created inside the article to achieve the desired improvement and undesirable signal factor above the specified band-width. The direct search approach is used to find the desired results for input and output matching networks.

articleTitle: Moth-Flame Optimization for Improving UWSNs Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This study aims to examine Moth-Flame Optimization (MFO) algorithm by proposing the use in improving the UWSNs system. UWSNs are indispensable for numerous underwater applications; nevertheless, they are confronted with several crucial hindrances, for example, bandwidth constraint, high-latency communication, and limited energy. Since these are complex problems, optimizing them using various techniques Presents a big challenge that could be addressed by bio-inspired optimization algorithms such as the MFO. The motivation for the development of MFO, which emulates the flight pattern moths for navigation, is to aid in the determination of optimal node positioning, routing path, and energy usage in the case of UWSNs. MATLAB workflow includes data collection, algorithm customization, and simulation and forms the basis of the overall methodology applied in the study. A comparison is made with regards to parameters such as network lifetime, energy utilization, data transmission success rate and delay using criteria such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The performance comparisons made between the proposed MFO algorithm and the traditional GA and PSO algorithms prove MFO to be highly effective attaining higher values for all the considered parameters. Thereby, the results demonstrate that the use of MFO has significant promise for increasing the UWSNs lifetime and reliability, making the technique more suitable for underwater surveillance and investigation. It is important for interested researchers and practitioners to understand how some of these bio-inspired optimization techniques can be employed in complex scenarios such as UWSNs, and how this research can inform future work in this area.

articleTitle: Detection of Gastric Cancer in Endoscopic Images Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: In finding features of gastric cancer in endoscopic images, difficulties arise from early manifestations and variance in the appearance of lesions. The objective of this study is to design an automobile deep convolutional neural network (CNN) that would help enhance the rate of accurate diagnosis of gastric cancer. In the current work, using the dataset of endoscopic images reviewed by senior gastroenterologists, transfer learning is applied on the base of the ResNet-50 based deep CNN the result of data augmentation is extended. By evaluating the model on measures of training, validation, and testing sets, high performance has been realized as depicted by accuracy of 87. 4%, precision of 87. 5%, recall of 87%, and f1-score of 87%. Research on the comparison of the proposed method with the conventional CAD systems and machine learning models confirmed the efficiency of the deep learning method. The utilization of Grad-CAM visualizations brought interpretability in improving match between regions of focus and clinically relevant areas therefore improving the trust in the model among the clinicians. To foster efficiency, the implementation incorporated Python and deep learning tools, including TensorFlow, the model of which was trained on GPUs. Thus, this paper demonstrates the feasibility of the studied CNNs in promoting the early diagnosis of gastric cancer, suggesting the adaptation of AI tools as complementary tools for clinicians in everyday practice. Future studies should follow up on how false negative results may occur; additionally, future studies should devise better approaches on how to increase the generalizability of these models across different patients.

articleTitle: Regeneration Sites Selection and Regenerator Assignment Strategies for Translucent Elastic Optical Networks: Survey and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Elastic Optical Networks (EONs) form the backbone of the present day Internet. In Translucent EONs (T-EONs), optical signals are propagated beyond their transparent reach and so in order to maintain the desired Quality of Transmission (QoT) level, the signals have to undergo 3R (re-shaping, re-timing and re-amplification) regeneration at some nodes designated as regeneration sites, also called regenerators. So identification of regenerators is an important problem and is known as Regeneration Site Selection (RSS) problem. Once the regenerators are identified, an important problem is the assignment of optical signals to these regenerators to meet various objectives of the network operator such as minimizing total used spectrum, total number of regenerations etc. and is known as the Regenerator Assignment (RA) problem. In this paper we extend two RSS algorithms originally designed for traditional translucent Wavelength Division Multiplexed (WDM) optical networks to make them applicable for Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) based T-EONs. We further study and analyses two RA algorithms. In addition, we present a survey of the various RSS and RA strategies for T-EONs available in the literature and thereby identify the future scope of research.

articleTitle: Direction of Arrival Estimation using Positive and Negative Harmonics of Time-Modulated Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Estimation of the received signal direction using time-modulated array (TMA) is getting more attention because of its inherent advantages of simple electronically controllable beamforming network. In this paper, two parameters based on the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> positive and negative harmonics of TMA with unipolar pulse sequence are employed to evaluate the direction of arrival (DoA) of the received signal and their performances over the feasible scanning range are investigated. It is observed that the parameter with negative harmonic component provides better accuracy in estimating DoA towards the positive side of the scanning range while the parameter with positive harmonic component is more precise towards the negative side. The numerical results corresponding to the accuracy of finding DoA in the form of root mean square error (RMSE) as obtained via Monte Carlo Simulation are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Gain of Rectangular Microstrip Antenna Through Metamaterial Inclusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: In order to improve the antenna's gain and alter its radiation properties, this study examines a rectangular microstrip patch antenna that is partially loaded with homogeneous substrate and superstrate made of μ-negative, ε-negative, and double negative metamaterials. The inclusion of proper size of double negative and μ-negative materials substrate can enhance the gain of antenna and control the resonant frequency. It is seen that embedded double negative substrate on either side of the patch substrate along its radiating edge result is increasing the antenna gain to about 10dBi as well as dual band operation where as embedded μ-negative substrate on the patch exhibit enhancement of gain as high as 9.50 dBi. The gain is hike compare to simple double positive substrate of rectangular microstrip patch antenna which is about 6 dBi. For a certain height of negative permeability material the gain is moderate similar to that obtained by double negative superstrate.

articleTitle: IoT Enabled Anti-Child Trafficking System Using Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of child trafficking in the South particularly in Bangladesh, India, and Nepal requires a creative solution that can go beyond the orthodox preventative techniques. This continuously growing issue mainly violates the fundamental rights of children, for example liberty, education, social support, and economic opportunities. Trafficked children must go through physical and sexual abuse, which turns into slavery, forced labor, and committing crimes like begging, theft, and delivering drugs. To create a definitive system that targets detecting and response for stopping child abduction and trafficking, this research provides an anti-child trafficking device that is embedded with different types of sensors and location trackers. These sensors are used to collect accurate data or information for real-time child monitoring. The collected data can be used for detecting potential trafficking routes and predicting future circumstances. Using these technologies, it is possible to create a protective boundary for children. This research paper presents a model of combined sensors of our proposed wearable device. It can be considered a resolver in the prevention of child trafficking and abduction, by providing any alert or messages to the parents now.

articleTitle: Attention-based Deep Learning model for Indoor Object Recognition Framework for Visually Impaired Individuals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: An enhanced indoor object identification structure for visually impaired individuals is utilized in this study. In order to create a more feature-rich training image, the RGB and depth pictures are initially collective using an Information Translation Module (ITM). The combined images are used to build feature maps using the Attentional Dense201 model. Using the help of RPNs and SIG Convs, the network is able to better understand spatial relationships. Acquisition of ROI data is accomplished through the use of perception-dependent ROI pooling. The network's fully linked layer then uses the inputs to detect objects. The hyperparameters of the framework are adjusted using an IGOA algorithm. The proposed framework tests and trains on the SUN RGB-D dataset. Several existing approaches are contrasted with the proposed model to assess the efficacy of the model. The proposed model has a testing accuracy of 96.35% and a frame processing time of 0.083 seconds, outperforming all previous models.

articleTitle: Two-order Wavelet Transform-Based Dual-Tamper Detection and Self-Restoration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: In this research, we propose a neat dual-tampering detection approach to further retrieve the forged content of 1080p images. The recovering of actual information is derived from the low-frequency components of the second-order wavelet. The procedure initiates with the segmentation of the image into a non-underlying section. To make better the quality of the recuperate image, a radially symmetrical mapping technique is employed to safeguard the recovery bits. The most notable bit-plane of each segment is utilized to generate the first component authentication key through the MD5 algorithm, while the second component authentication key is produced using SHA1 based on the recovered data. Subsequently, the watermarked image is formed by embedding the recovery bits and the dual authentication keys into the least significant bits of the original image. During the tampering detection phase, the calculated authentication keys are compared against the retrieved keys. Any discrepancies result in the block being classified as tampered. Following this, centrosymmetric mapping is applied to extract the low-frequency coefficients of the second-order wavelet for the purpose of image self-recovery. The inverse wavelet transform is then executed to restore the tampered regions with the recovery data, thereby finalizing the self-recovery process. Our experimental findings indicate that this approach yields enhanced recovery quality and more effectively conceals the embedded information.

articleTitle: Bioinspired Routing Protocols for UWSNs Using Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The aim of this research therefore is to propose and design bio-inspired routing protocols in UWSNs using PSO. High latency and low bandwidth, coupled with high error rates, make underwater routing a different ball game than routing in normal situations and traditional mediums. The proposed PSO-based protocols also consider factors like power utilization, coverage distance, and priority of data packets to make better routing choices thus helping to improve the efficiency and responsiveness of the UWSNs. The compare analysis of the proposed protocols with the earlier protocols, which are also developed based on AODV and DSR, proves high performance of the PSO based protocols in the energy consumption, data delivery ratio, end to end delay and the network lifetime within all the realistic underwater environments analyzed by the simulations. Such advancement would help to improve the communication system in UWSNs, presenting new approaches for efficient communication in the underwater environment.

articleTitle: Estimation And Analysis of Power Consumption & Gate Delay of Product of Sum Function Based Digital Integrated Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This work represents design and simulation of a CMOS digital VLSI circuit based on a Product of Sum (POS) expression using both Static and Dynamic CMOS design techniques. The proposed circuits have been designed and simulated at 180nm and 150nm CMOS technology nodes. The circuit’s functionality has been verified using of the T-SPICE tools. Gate delay, power consumption & power delay product (PDP) have been estimated to compare the impact of different design techniques. The variation of supply voltage from 0.6 V to 1.5 V has been considered to represent power delay analysis. The T-SPICE simulation results depicts that the optimum values of PDPs for Static CMOS circuit are 7.364aJ and 0.374aJ for 180nm and 150nm technology node respectively at VDD value 1V. The dynamic CMOS circuit offer lower optimum values of PDPs as 1.773aJ and 0.092aJ for 180nm and 150nm technology node respectively at VDD values 1.1V and 0.6V. Thus, this work may be useful for digital VLSI designer for the power delay analysis of VLSI circuits.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Classification in Mammograms Using Support Vector Machines (SVMs) and Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This work focuses on breast cancer classification in mammograms using SVMs classifier and histogram of oriented gradients features. The envisioned system is designed in such a way to enhance the diagnostic precision through integration of the virtues of both SVMs and HOG in identifying discriminative characteristics of breast tissue. Special emphasis was given on comparing and testing the performance of the intended model with other models on a public mammogram dataset containing both malignant and benign cases; the optimized SVM model provided an accuracy of 92%. 5%, sensitivity of 91. 0%, specificity of 93. 74 (fig 5) and 8%, and an AUC-ROC of 0. 95. This study shows that the method is efficient in discriminating between the malignant and benign first axillary lymph node tissue. The developed CAD system was found to possess the prospect of becoming a valuable support system for radiologists in the early detection of breast cancer. Keywords: Breast cancer; Mammograms; Support Vector Machines; Histogram of Oriented Gradient Descent; Computer-aided diagnosis.

articleTitle: Tuning of Photocurrent by Magnetic Field in p-Si/NiFe2O4/CuPc/Au Heterostructure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: We have successfully fabricated p-Si/NiFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> (NFO)/CuPc/Au heterostructure and have investigated its photocurrent under the influence of magnetic field. Upon exposure to 660 nm red laser light, the photocurrent exhibits an increase corresponding to the rise in optical power. When both light and magnetic fields are applied, the photocurrent to dark current ratio initially increases and then decreases with the magnetic field at a constant positive bias. Furthermore, with the application of magnetic field a significant change in the electrical hysteresis width (|ΔI|) is observed when the heterostructure is under optical illumination compared to when it is in dark condition. This change in |ΔI| may result from the reorientation of magnetic clusters and magnetostriction caused by the applied magnetic field. This heterostructure has potential for future development in advanced opto-spintronics sensor devices.

articleTitle: Automatic Lung Tumor Volume Estimation Using PSO-TSVM Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This research is driven by concerns over the increasing cost of patient care and demand for faster clinical interventions. It is based on the prime hypothesis that well-trained machine learning models can be used to improve the accuracy of pathology localization. A well-tested, robust and accurate model for tumor volume measurement and segmentation. The proposed method uses CT scans for diagnosis and combines particle swarm optimization with twin support vector machine to detect the lung infection. A two-stage framework called Suspicious Volumetric Tumor Segmentation (SVTS) following a segmentation classification pipeline is proposed for classification of normal and abnormal tumorous lung CT slices from a standard dataset.
