The experiments conducted on the dataset given the better result when compared to other machine learning methods. The performance of the proposed method measured by accuracy, precision, sensitivity, error rate and F1-Score. The proposed method achieves 96.18 % accuracy.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection of Cardiac Arrhythmias using Discrete Wavelet Transform and Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Cardiac diseases are a leading cause of mortality globally, necessitating early diagnosis for effective treatment and better patient outcomes. Electrocardiography (ECG) is a widely used diagnostic tool that provides critical insights into the heart's bioelectrical activity. Advances in machine learning have enabled the development of automated systems for detecting cardiac diseases from ECG signals, enhancing timely diagnosis and patient care. This study introduces a method for identifying arrhythmias by employing a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier, with feature extraction performed on filtered electrocardiogram (ECG) signals using the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). The model was validated with 3672 ECG datasets from GitHub, using 2931 signals for training and 741 for validation and testing. The model achieved high accuracy, with training and testing accuracies of 99.35% and 97.84%, respectively. Confusion matrix analysis showed minimal misclassification for both training and testing datasets. With an SVM accuracy of 99.3% for arrhythmia detection, the proposed system outperforms other models such as Decision Tree (95.2%), Artificial Neural Network (97.3%), and Random Forest (94.6%). This research highlights the effectiveness of combining DWT and SVM for precise early detection of arrhythmias, helping to lower the risk of severe complications like stroke and cardiac arrest.

articleTitle: Real-time Traffic Prediction in 5G Networks Using LSTM Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This research explores the application of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for real-time traffic prediction within 5G networks, aiming to address the critical need for accurate prediction models in dynamic network environments. Leveraging the sequential learning capabilities of LSTM networks, the proposed methodology encompasses dataset preparation, model architecture design, training, and evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the LSTM-based prediction model in capturing temporal dependencies and providing reliable predictions across various prediction horizons. While promising, further research is warranted to enhance the model's performance and address remaining challenges. This study contributes to advancing the state-of-the-art in traffic prediction methodologies, facilitating more efficient network management and optimization in 5G environments.

articleTitle: A high isolation SIW based Self-diplexing antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: In this research paper, a SIW-based two-port self diplexing antenna is planned for design with isolation (high). The antenna is sourced by two coaxial feed lines to radiate at operating frequencies 4.75 GHz and 5.65 GHz. A high isolation of 40 dB is achieved by making a triangular shield between the two resonators. The given Triangular shielded high-isolation self-diplexing antenna (TSHISDA) has high inter-port isolation, peak realized gains of 5.2 dBi and 6.2 dBi, and better radiation properties.

articleTitle: A non linear system controlling by using artificial neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This article describes using artificial neural networks (ANNs) to control nonlinear systems. A third-order function is used to represent the nonlinear system. Using back propagation delay, the ANN has been utilized to train the nonlinear system's unknown variable. The fact that the non-linear system is non-converging indicates that it is an unstable, non-bounded system. Enhancement of the performance parameters is possible if the third-order system's objective function incorporates the limitations limits. ANN is used to train the third order non-linear system with restrictions. The nonlinear system is rapidly convergent to a bounded value in the stable area following the use of ANN.

articleTitle: Mathematical Models of Heterogeneous Machine Learning Techniques for Ransomware Protection in Cyber-Physical Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Ransomware attacks are a growing threat to cyber-physical systems (CPS), capable of causing financial losses, downtime, and even physical harm. Using machine learning to detect and prevent these attacks is a promising approach. A study compared four machine learning techniques—support vector machines (SVM), decision trees, random forests, and neural networks—to detect ransomware attacks on CPS. The models were trained and evaluated using a dataset of real ransomware incidents. Results showed that all four techniques effectively detected ransomware attacks. Neural networks achieved the highest F1 score, while SVMs excelled in precision, recall, and accuracy. However, the differences in performance among the methods were not significant. The models detected ransomware outbreaks within an average of 12 hours, allowing businesses to mitigate the attack's effects promptly. The study concluded that machine learning could effectively detect and prevent ransomware attacks on CPS. However, it is important to note that the study used a limited dataset, highlighting the need for further research with larger datasets to confirm these findings.

articleTitle: Emerging Applications of FinFET's in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Hardwares
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: FinFET technology, a groundbreaking leap in semiconductor design, has substantially affected the buildup of hardware for the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) applications. This study investigates the developing uses of FinFETs in AI and ML hardware, explaining their high-quality fulfillment, power efficiency, and scalability. As AI and ML algorithms demand greater computing capacity, FinFETs offer a solid answer by raising processing speed and accuracy as they lowering power consumption. This study explores numerous applications among them neuromorphic computer technology, edge AI devices, and computing performance for ML training. It also includes FinFET-based methodology case studies, demonstrating their distinct benefits over antiquated technology. Although FinFETs may have manufacturing issues and constraints, they will advance technology for ML and AI. This study emphasizes FinFET technology's crucial role in satisfying AI and ML demands, enabling further along efficient and effective hardware solutions.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Design Optimization of FinFET Transistors for Energy-Efficient Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This study addresses the application of machine learning approaches to increase the efficacy of the FinFET transistor approach with the objective of increasing energy use in computing workloads. The adoption of FinFET technology is vital in establishing energy-efficient computer systems due to its enhanced electrostatic control and lower leakage currents. However, in order to attain the optimum degree of performance, it is required to make accurate alterations to distinct design aspects, which could be challenging when applying traditional approaches. In this research, we provide a new solution that leverages neural network techniques to ease the design optimization method. Using the training of models on complete datasets documenting FinFET characteristics and performance indicators, we disclose remarkable advances in energy efficiency and computational capabilities. Our observations not only indicate the efficacy of machine learning in faster FinFET design optimization but also underline its potential in spurring invention across energy-efficient computing systems. This study adds to the improvement of contemporary semiconductor design methodologies, providing doors for ecologically sound and high-performing computing systems.

articleTitle: Developing Algorithms for Predicting Gene-Disease Associations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: It is evident that identifying gene-disease relationships is essential to elucidate disease genomics and progression as well as aiding in developing targeted therapies. This work aims at training and testing various machine learning approaches for predicting these relations, as well as considering various datasets, and their integration involving multi-omics data. The process of data collection has been carried out from Genomic, Transcriptomic, and Clinical data stored in various data repositories and then preprocessed for feature selection and fine-tuning of the model along with the development of Supervised, Unsupervised, and Integrated Models. The models were built and tested using cross-validated data sets; model efficiency was assessed with respect to accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score. The findings showed that the models from the second group of hybrids obtained a systematically higher accuracy than models from the first and subsequent groups, especially when analyzing multiple types of ‘omics data at once. Similar deployments on entirely separate datasets ensured the model’s reliability and portability across different contexts. Furthermore, interpretability features and visualization modules were included into the software to improve assessment and interactivity for users and scholars. This research will be beneficial for the field of genomics since it proposes tools that will help in the better understanding of disease and the identification of genes involved in particular diseases, making it possible to start the process of targeting important genes in order to develop cures for such diseases. The study results preaciously highlight the significance of applying integrated strategies of data and analytic methodology to improving the accuracy of the prediction and implementing the personalized medicine concept.

articleTitle: Probabilistic and Interpretable Approach for Malaria Transmission Forecasting via ARIMA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The current Malaria outbreak poses a significant global challenge for healthcare systems worldwide. Each day, new and intricate datasets emerge, detailing positive and negative case counts, hospital admissions, mortality rates, bed occupancy, ventilator shortages, and more. Infections surge notably during the rainy season, underscoring the urgent need for early detection and forecasting techniques to curb disease transmission and facilitate a swift and safe resumption of economic activities. A model was devised utilizing classical mathematical modeling methods, employing exponential regression, to forecast infection spread. The accuracy of these forecasts was assessed, revealing limitations in predicting infection spread beyond a two-week timeframe. Results underscore the efficacy of the ARIMA model for short-term forecasting, enabling timely public health responses and evidence-based interventions crucial for effective disease management and containment. Leveraging automated model selection processes and precise performance evaluation metrics enhances the reliability and applicability of forecasting tools in real-world healthcare scenarios, aiding decision-making and resource allocation strategies.

articleTitle: Towards Sustainable Waste Management: EfficientNetB0 Garbage Classification Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The swift rise in trash production in recent times has presented formidable obstacles to efficient garbage handling and ecological sustainability. Conventional garbage sorting techniques are labor-intensive and frequently imprecise, which increases environmental contamination and inefficiency in recycling operations. The EfficientNetB0 rubbish Sorter, a cutting-edge deep learning-based system intended to transform waste management through automated and incredibly precise rubbish classification, is presented in this paper. Known for its optimal performance and computational efficiency, the EfficientNetB0 model is used to categorize different waste materials into different categories, including organic trash, paper, plastic, metal, and glass. The model maintains a low computational footprint and produces higher classification accuracy by using a huge dataset of tagged garbage photos for fine-tuning and transfer learning. The EfficientNetB0 Garbage Sorter outperforms existing approaches, as demonstrated by experimental findings, which show an excellent classification accuracy of over 99%. Extensive testing is also used to confirm the system's resilience to changes in trash appearance and its generalizability across various waste types. Furthermore, the model's practical application in automated garbage sorting facilities is guaranteed by its real-time categorization capacity. By using the EfficientNetB0 Garbage Sorter, waste sorting operations will be more effective overall, requiring less manual work, and waste sorting activities will be more efficient. This novel approach advances the overarching objectives of sustainable resource management and environmental preservation by enabling more precise and effective trash classification.

articleTitle: Segmentation of Retinal Blood Vessels in Fundus Images Using Fully Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Segmentation is mandatory to analyze retinal blood vessel indication for diagnosis of various ophthalmic and systemic disorders. This paper takes a look at this problem, specifically, the application of Fully Convolutional Networks (FCNs) in this whole process, with a primary focus on the U-Net architecture. In this work, the authors conduct the experiments on three datasets, namely DRIVE, STARE and CHASE_DB1, and prepare the images for modeling through normalization, resizing, and data augmentation. Due to the binary structure of the task, the loss function of the proposed method is binary cross-entropy along with the Dice coefficient, and the model is trained with the Adam optimizer. The improvement scores that was obtained shows that the proposed model has a high accuracy, precision, recall and F1 score on all the datasets used and has proven to be better than other existing methods. The study establishes the usefulness of FCNs in segmenting the tree structure of the retinal blood vessel structures in uniterrupted manner, and presented promising improvement for early diagnosis and treatment in the clinical application. it emphasizes on the necessity of utilizing far improved deep learning architectures and more holistic training mechanisms in striving to create more accurate diagnosis support systems in medical image analysis.

articleTitle: Variance Score and Pearson Similarity based Unsupervised Feature Selection (VPUFS) for Sample Clustering in Microarray Gene Expression Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The analysis of high-dimensional gene profiles plays a vital part in cancer research, facilitating early detection, ameliorated prognostic, and the development of targeted therapeutic strategies. Grouping of similar data samples based on their gene profiles can be very beneficial for new cancer class identification. However, the high dimensionality and complexity of these gene profile data pose significant computational challenges, necessitating innovative approaches for feature selection and data reduction. This study proposes a novel framework called ‘Variance Score and Pearson Similarity based Unsupervised Feature Selection (VPUFS)’, a feature selection fashion to choose relevant features, for reducing high dimensionality of unlabeled datasets, thereby helping as a preprocessing step to cluster cancer samples effectively. The unsupervised dimensionality reduction framework leverages variance to calculate feature class relevance score, and similarity metrics to identify and retain informative features while eliminating the redundant ones. The proposed framework is rigorously evaluated across multiple gene profiles, such as, Leukemia, Prostate, Breast and Colon cancer samples. Comparative evaluations demonstrate that the proposed methodology outperforms existing feature selection techniques from unlabeled gene profiles, thus showing an enhanced stability and improved classification and clustering accuracies.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Techniques for Protein Structure Prediction in Bioinformatics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This work analyses and discusses the use of machine learning methods in the field of bioinformatics concerning protein structure prediction. The steps of the proposed methodology include: acquiring and cleaning the relevant proteins sequences datasets; and creation and training of deep learning models, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and Recurrent Neural Networks, (RNNs). Overall, adding data augmentation and transfer learning boosts the performance of the models to a mean accuracy of 87%. Predictors Evaluation: In evaluating the predictors, the model used an accuracy of 6% and a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0. 74. The generality and efficiency of the proposed model are tested and compared with results from other similar standard datasets. Study shows that the results of the model have higher reliability than the traditional method of the machine-learning algorithm especially in the classification of the second and third levels of varied types of proteins. The research will demonstrate the applicability and possibility of the large-scale and cost-efficient approaches to the protein structure prediction using machine learning, while emphasizing the drawbacks of experimental tools. Recommendations for future work are to enhance the interpretability of the resulting models, better combine methods based on the use of information from hybrid schemes with physical models, and use more extensive databases for enhancing accuracy. This research highlights the profound impact that machine learning can have in the field of bioinformatics as a tool to enhance knowledge of such protein structures and to further practice improvements in the understanding of life processes and a and drug design.

articleTitle: Android Malware Detection Using Deep Transfer Learning Model for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The rapid increase in Internet of Things (IoT) devices has heightened concerns about Android malware threats, demanding more sophisticated intrusion detection methods. This paper introduces an innovative approach focused on pinpointing and classifying Android malware, specifically designed to address challenges within IoT applications. Leveraging Deep Transfer Learning, our model utilizes pre-trained neural networks to effectively extract intricate features crucial for distinguishing diverse malware types. This method ensures enhanced accuracy in identifying malware strains. By employing deep transfer learning, our model adeptly addresses the evolving landscape of Android malware threats, especially within IoT setups. Evaluation involved rigorous experiments on three established Android malware datasets—Malgenome, AAGM, and Drebin—emphasizing accuracy and F-score metrics. For the Malgenome dataset, it is observed that the proposed algorithm achieved an accuracy of 98.02% and an F-score of 96.99% at a dataset size of 20. For the AAGM dataset, the proposed algorithm achieved an accuracy of 95.09% and an F-score of 94.23%. For the Drebin dataset, the proposed algorithm achieved an accuracy of 97.89% and an F-score of 95.07%. Results unequivocally showcase our model's proficiency in accurately discerning and categorizing Android malware, even amidst varying dataset sizes. Significantly improved accuracy and F-scores were observed compared to traditional machine learning methods.

articleTitle: Precision Segmentation and Feature Extraction of Blood Vessels of Retina using Automated Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: To mitigate the shortcomings of manual vessel segmentation of bloods in retinal images, an automatic algorithm is proposed to enhance diagnosis accuracy and reduce ophthalmologists' workload. The developed procedure for segmenting blood vessels of retinal fundus images has two sections: Image Partitioning and Attribute Extraction. Comprehensive experiments using different (DRIVE, HRF) datasets assessed the algorithm's performance in detecting retinal vessels of blood. Five quantitative metric performances parameters—accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value and negative predictive value—were validated through calculations of its efficiency against current state-of-the-art methods on the dataset used (DRIVE).The introduced technique for extracting blood vessels of retinal fundus images has some mentionable improvement by scoring an Accuracy, Sensitivity, Specificity, PPV, and NPV.

articleTitle: Predictive Analytics for Network Traffic Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: It examines how this can be applied to monitoring network traffic and carrying out predictive analysis to improve the functionality and effectiveness of network management. The study uses historical data of the network traffics and uses machine learning techniques such as the Long Short Term Memory based models and the Ensemble Methods to predict the traffic patterns in the future. It includes data gathering, data pre-processing, feature selection, model choice, model training, model validation, and the architectural setup of the machine learning solution in a real-time stream processing pipeline using Apache Kafka and Apache Flink. It is evident from the results that the proposed models yield a high level of accuracy in terms of prediction and that the Ensemble method alone gives a slightly higher accuracy than LSTM in the specific metrics. Real-time values closely followed actual traffic level, thus allowing real-time adjustments in network usage. In light of this, there is a clear understanding of the significance of having reliable data preprocessing, feature engineering, and model optimization process. The study also notes the need in prediction concerning data quality and scalability issues taking into account that current and future networks are characterized as dynamic and highly complex to offer more effective solutions for intelligent and proactive networking.

articleTitle: NLP and ML for real-time sentiment analysis in Finance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The integration of Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) is pivotal in stock market analysis, enabling the extraction of meaningful insights from vast quantities of news articles, social media feeds, and financial reports. NLP techniques assist in distilling sentiments, tendencies, and crucial market information from unstructured text, thus equipping investors with the knowledge to make well-informed decisions. Machine learning algorithms leverage historical data to forecast market trends, refine trading strategies, and assess risk factors. This synergy of NLP and ML offers investors rapid and precise data analysis, critical for navigating the complex terrain of modern financial markets. This study evaluates the effectiveness of a classification model designed to categories data into distinct groups. Essential metrics used to measure the model’s performance include accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, support, and log loss. The model demonstrates a precision rate of 78% and a recall rate of 94%, indicating its proficiency in correctly identifying and classifying data points. The F1-score, a harmonic mean of precision and recall, stands at 0.85, highlighting the model’s balanced capability. The support score, which accounts for the number of occurrences in the dataset, is 31, providing an insight into the dataset’s composition. Furthermore, the log loss value of 0.42 reflects the model’s predictive accuracy. Collectively, these performance metrics validate the model’s effectiveness and relevance in stock market analysis.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Network Intrusion Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This study aims at analyzing and outlining an AI-based NIDS design and comparing different implementation models to improve the current state of network protection. Current NIDS do not assist organizations against modern cyber threats hence relies on machine learning and deep learning for real-time protections. The detailed plan of work includes the use of signature and anomaly detection techniques in parallel and the use of ensemble technique for increasing the detectors capabilities and decrease the false positive rates. The study employs open datasets for training and benchmarking and establishes that deep learning models, including CNNs and RNNs, elicit improved results compared to more conventional machine learning models. The results show that the ensemble learning model, outperformed the other and thus emphasizes future work should consider the use of this model for detection of network intrusions. This study shows that netsec based on AI-powered NIDS can increase the opportunity to detect threats and effectively respond to incidents in realistic network contexts. Further research by designs will involve handling issues like model interpretability and updates to sustain reliability and scalability.

articleTitle: EPD-ECNN: Enhanced PCOS Detection with Preprocessed Ultrasound Images and Ensemble CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a prevalent hormonal disorder in women of reproductive age, characterized by irregular menstrual cycles and elevated androgen levels, significantly impacting fertility. PCOS is also associated with conditions such as acne, hair loss, excessive hair growth, elevated androgens, and infrequent ovulation. Traditionally, PCOS diagnosis is performed manually by gynecologists through the labor-intensive and subjective process of counting and measuring ovarian follicles. Recently, Machine Learning (ML) approaches for PCOS detection have gained traction due to their potential for more accurate and early diagnosis, minimizing health risks for women. While various ML models for PCOS detection exist, they often overlook the importance of preprocessing, which is essential for developing robust and reliable models. This study introduces the EPD-ECNN model for detecting PCOS from ultrasound images. First, image quality is enhanced using the CLAHE technique. Then, images are segmented using the watershed algorithm. The model combines pre-trained CNNs, specifically InceptionV3 and DenseNet121, for feature extraction. Finally, a fully connected layer is used for classification. The EPD-ECNN model achieved an accuracy of 98.59%, demonstrating its efficiency in medical cases of PCOS detection.

articleTitle: VisionaryX-9: Efficient plant disease prediction model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Agriculture, which is the foundation of worldwide sustenance, is facing substantial obstacles in the twenty-first century, mainly because of increasing demands for food production and the growing menace of plant diseases. Ensuring the well-being of crops is of utmost importance for the security of global food supply, which requires the timely and precise detection of plant diseases. Conventional approaches are becoming less effective in dealing with the changing agricultural dangers, necessitating the development of new and creative solutions. The incorporation of machine learning and deep learning technologies in recent agricultural practices has significantly transformed plant disease diagnosis, providing remarkable levels of accuracy, efficiency, and scalability. This study utilises advanced algorithms such as ResNet, VGG, and EfficientNet to improve the accuracy of disease identification, thereby revolutionising precision agriculture. The main objective of this article is to enhance the process of plant disease detection with the help of a sophisticated model, VisonaryX-9, that can not only properly identify plant diseases but also classify their symptoms. The objective is to empower farmers by furnishing them with timely information, enabling informed decisions that directly influence agricultural output and, consequently, global food production. Our contributions consist of the creation of VisonaryX-9, a hybrid model that merges the ResNet and VGG architectures. The model is validated with a dataset of having 87,295 real-world plant disease images. The results obtained indicates the the model outperforms other baseline model with an accuracy of 99.12%. Our objective is to reveal profound understandings that will enhance the discussion on sustainable and resilient farming methodologies.

articleTitle: ML-Based Financial Forecasting in ERP: Improving Budgeting Accuracy with Long Short-Term Memory Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This research examines the feasibility of using LSTM networks for financial prediction in frameworks such as the ERP system with an objective of enhancing budgetary prediction. Simple forecasting techniques do not take into account certain dynamics within the data that are non-linear, hence result in small forecast accuracy. Autoencoders can be employed to extract such features and LSTM networks capable of handling sequential data and long term dependencies could be used to anticipate the occurrence of emergencies. The process includes data culling that is composed of extensive datasets, data pre-processing, LSTM model development and training, and ERP system implementation. The findings illustrate that by extending the number of timesteps in LSTM models, it offers more reliability compared to conventional methods that help to improve decision-making and forecasting in finance. It is possible to upgrade them from time to time and make the models as accurate and as current as possible. These specific findings corroborate the overall proposition that discrete advancements in ML algorithms can converge to radically reshape a key area of ERP systems – financial forecasting.

articleTitle: Smart Card-Based Mutual Authentication Mechanism for UAV Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The frequency and severity of disasters have increased, necessitating robust monitoring and response systems over the years. Unmanned Aerial vehicles (UAVs), integrated into the Internet of Drones (IoDs), play a crucial role in real-time disaster management. This study proposes a mutual authentication mechanism for UAV networks based on smart cards, which emphasizes security and low computing overhead. Hashes and EX-OR operations guarantee efficient and secure communication, tackling important threats like impersonation, Man-In-the-Middle, identity guessing, etc. Additionally, our Scyther tool and BAN logic simulation ensures that private information is protected when producing a shared key. Results are compared to relatable authentication techniques, and protocol performance exceeds prior research. Emergency data transfer is quicker due to the protocol's minimal computing costs.

articleTitle: An IoT and Machine Learning Approach to In-Home Elderly Care
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The recent increase in the global aging population has resulted in many social and economic challenges for elderly people at the familial level. The inability to provide continuous and urgent care in domestic environments has resulted in a lack of independence among the elderly. This has further increased the burden on family members and caregivers. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an IoT and machine learning-based solution to monitor multiple health parameters of the aged individuals. The proposed system is designed implemented using a wearable sensing device integrated with in-style data visualization and analysis. The device allows medical practitioners and caregivers to access real-time and historical data on a patient for general monitoring and to provide obligatory care. With further use of machine learning techniques, the system is able to predict heart conditions with 65% accuracy in an elderly patient.

articleTitle: Adaptive Beamforming in MIMO Systems Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: One of the most significant procedures in MIMO system is the adaptive beamforming which is the technique of adjusting the direction of signal transmission for better wireless communication. This paper aims to investigate the application of deep learning in combination with adaptive beamforming for the improvement of the existing technologies and techniques having some limitations which prove efficient when working in certain applications and scenarios only. Utilizing the CNNs and RNNs, the proposed approach then determines ideal beamforming patterns from various datasets, synthetic simulations, as well as measured ones. In this paper, various approaches are employed which include the Super & Reinforcement learning techniques, which makes the deep learning-based models capable of learning in real-time the change of channel characteristics. Simulations and practical adaptations of changing protocols have illustrated substantial enhancements on SINR, BER, and system capacity. The conclusion indicates that the proposed DL based technique is better than the existing standards providing more considerably higher data rates with reasonable less error rates and possessing highly adaptive capability. From the literature, it is clear that deep learning has a significant use in adaptive beam forming; although it has significantly increased the computational load. For future wireless communication technologies such as 5G and beyond MIMO systems this work has demonstrated the promises of deep learning to improve such systems.

articleTitle: A Modified Linknet Architecture for Attack Detection in Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: As the IoT continues to proliferate across various domains, ensuring the security of IoT networks against malicious attacks remains a critical challenge. This work proposes a novel method to enhance the attack detection in IoT environments by employing a Modified LinkNet (MLinkNet) architecture. Addressing inherent challenges in existing methodologies, the SMOTE is employed to mitigate the class imbalance issue in IoT attack datasets, there by improving the model performance. The Modified Link Net model deviates from conventional encoder-decoder framework is introduced by integrating the fused pooling layers and an improved activation function designed to preserve high-resolution features critical for accurate attack identification. Rigorous experimentation on IoT attack datasets demonstrates superior detection accuracy and computational efficiency compared to traditional methods. This research contributes a robust solution to IoT security challenges, advancing the field with a scalable and effective model capable of adapting to emerging cyber threats in IoT ecosystems.

articleTitle: Improving Beamforming in 5G Networks Using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This paper presents a study on training of Reinforcement Learning (RL) for balancing of beamforming in 5G network. Major challenges in giving directions in traditional beamforming collapse in dynamic surroundings: Beamforming which plays an essential role in increasing the strength and quality of a signal. RL provides a solution by allowing system to discover that actions that lead to a favorable outcome in the environment. The research process will involve first having a 5G network emulation, designing a DQN for beamforming, and finally having a comparison with traditional methods or other established algorithms. Effects that are observed on signal-to-noise ratio and throughput, and latencies further showed that RL based beamforming yield enhanced results. This paper also captures the possibilities of RL in handling aspects of 5G network and the development of wireless communication.

articleTitle: Voltage profile enhancement and harmonic reduction in power system network using fuzzy logic controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This article investigates the condition of power in the power system network. High voltage profiles and elevated harmonics are the primary concerns associated with conventional power system networks. Total harmonic distortion is the metric used to quantify harmonics. The IEEE 14 bus system has been selected as the standard power system network. The IEEE 14 bus system has experienced unbalanced operation as a consequence of the 10% capacity increase on all buses. STATCOM was constructed to resolve these concerns, and its switching was managed by a fuzzy logic controller (FLC). In comparison to STATCOM without FLC, the voltage profile and THD (%) have been substantially enhanced when using the STATCOM-based FLC.

articleTitle: Enhancing Network Security: Deep Learning-Powered Intrusion Detection with Data Engineering Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The research work focuses on improving network security by integrating Deep Learning techniques, data engineering methodologies, and adaptive defensive measures. The context emphasizes the growing intricacy of cyber risks and the need for sophisticated Intrusion Detection System. The methods used include optimizing DL architectures via pruning and quantization, including ensemble learning, implementing dynamic data augmentation, and improving model interpretability. The observed findings show significant improvements in the performance of intrusion detection. The accuracy of the model climbed from 92.5% to 96.1%, the precision improved from 89.7% to 93.8%, the recall went from 94.2% to 97.2%, and the F1-score enhanced from 91.8% to 95.5%. These metrics indicate the system's capacity to identify and counteract incursions with greater precision and effectiveness. It enhances the methodical and efficient method of detecting intrusions, specifically targeting the ever-changing nature of cyber threats. The integrated architecture greatly improves the robustness and flexibility of IDS, allowing for the implementation of proactive defensive measures in contemporary network settings.

articleTitle: Enhanced Diabetes Prediction Using Salivary Enzymes and Machine Learning Techniques: A Comprehensive and Explainable Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Diabetes is a significant cause of death globally. People with diabetes are more susceptible to infections, possibly due to problems with their immune system. Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a disorder characterised by insufficient insulin production or ineffective utilisation of insulin, leading to elevated blood glucose levels. Timely identification of diabetes is essential for efficient control and therapy. Conventional techniques depend on intrusive blood testing, however recent advancements indicate that salivary enzymes can be used as non-invasive indicators. Using saliva for diagnosis is promising because collecting saliva is simple, doesn’t require invasive procedures, and is less technically demanding than drawing blood. Saliva is a special liquid that plays a crucial role in the mouth’s normal functioning. Detecting diabetes through blood tests can be challenging in certain groups like children, older adults, and those who are sick or weakened. This study introduces an improved framework for predicting diabetes by combining salivary enzymes with advanced machine learning algorithms and ensemble learning. To improve the model’s comprehensibility, we employed the Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) technique, which is a component of explainable AI (XAI). Multiple machine learning models are assessed using the Diabetes dataset, which comprises data from 300 patients. Simulation results reveal that XGBoost attains the maximum accuracy of 89% and elucidates the causes and variables contributing to diabetes, thereby assisting medical practitioners in decision-making for clinical diagnosis and treatment strategies.

articleTitle: Embedded Soft Computing Applications Using Low Power VLSI Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Energy deficit VLSI addresses are important for several purposes, especially in IC and microchip development. Energy-efficient, compact, and durable electronics require low-power VLSI addressing. Modern integrated circuit design must address power limits, temperature regulation, and environmental concerns. Soft computing is used in embedded systems. Soft computing is an AI discipline that develops intelligent systems that can handle uncertainty, imprecision, and imperfect truth. Soft computing uses approximation reasoning and probabilistic tactics to solve complex real-world problems instead of mathematical models. The work emphasizes low-power VLSI addressing for cost-effective and durable soft computing applications embedding. These low-power VLSI techniques in integrated soft computing applications can enhance battery life, energy utilization, and performance while maintaining precision and predictability. Low-power VLSI techniques in embedded soft computing systems enhance energy efficiency, battery life, cost, and dependability. These tactics encourage the development of cutting-edge, environmentally friendly embedded systems that can perform complex soft computing tasks within power constraints.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Technique in Next Generation Healthcare Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Advancement of science and technology makes human life very comfortable, healthy, and little bit secure. Current technology like Body Sensor Network, and Internet of Things, are making a healthcare system which is capable of detecting disease earlier on the basis of prior symptoms shown by the body. By using sensors we are now able to measure these symptoms like high or low blood pressure, body temperature, glucose level, heart beats, and more. Researchers are now incorporating the Artificial Intelligence with the next generation healthcare systems, making it a Self-Optimization system. In this paper, some advance technologies for healthcare system followed by some valuable artificial intelligence techniques are discussed. Based on some sorted research papers, author present a comparative analysis discussing about techniques used in next generation healthcare systems, objectives to achieve, and about the future aspects in terms of authors. Followed by these details, author also mention some applications, challenges and research trends in the field of healthcare system.

articleTitle: 5G Managed Services Induced Changes in Telecom Value Chain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This paper analyzes the transformative influence of managed services on the telecommunications value chain amidst the arrival of 5G technology. Managed services have assumed multifaceted roles within contemporary telecom markets, reshaping the value chain significantly over the past decades. However, their significance in the 5G era surpasses that of preceding mobile generations, endowing network vendors with increased authority. The evolution is primarily attributed to the introduction of novel technologies and provisions inherent in 5G networks. Unlike previous generations, network operators find themselves unable to independently construct their 5G infrastructure, thereby shifting the strategic landscape in favour of vendors. This paradigm shift underscores the pivotal role of specialized vendors in optimizing 5G networks to address the unique challenges posed by this high-speed, low-latency technology. Managed services integration in 5G heralds a paradigmatic shift in telecom value chains, revolutionizing network design, deployment, and maintenance methodologies. In addition to traditional responsibilities, managed service providers now contribute to network security, proactive monitoring, and dynamic optimization, ensuring heightened reliability and efficiency. This transformative impact empowers vendors to navigate the complex telecom landscape and unlock the full potential of 5G technologies.

Author Keywords: impact of managed services on telecom value chain

articleTitle: Indoor 3D REM Design using Ordinary Kriging Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: This study examines three-dimensional (3D) and two-dimensional (2D) interpolation approaches for indoor 3D radio environment map (REM), on received signal strength (RSS) data of ultrahigh frequency (UHF) active television (TV) channel, to explore indoor TV white space (TVWS) volumes. It could serve as a valuable resource for cognitive radio operations during unlicensed secondary access indoors. A significant portion of data traffic originates indoors. Altitude considerations or realistic view of indoor radio environment map could improve the detection of TVWS volumes, thereby boosting channel data rates and throughput, which are crucial in secondary access. The measured 3D RSS dataset assisted spatial interpolation, exponential and spherical semivariogram (SV) models based 3D and 2D ordinary kriging (OK), results evaluation has been done on two metrics - computation time (CT) and root mean square error (RMSE). Performance comparison of the spherical and exponential SV model for 3D and 2D OK, reveals that the spherical model outperforms the exponential model to a moderate extent for 3D-OK, while the exponential model marginally outdoes the spherical model in 2D-OK. Study finds that 3D-OK yields lower RMSE values compared to 2D-OK for spherical and exponential SV. The analysis indicates that 3D-OK achieves 17.41% and 13.98% higher accuracy using the spherical and exponential SV than 2D-OK. The CT of 3D-OK is 1.09 times faster than the 2D-OK. The best-tracked TVWS volume is 18200m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, 7.624% of the real building volume. The findings suggest considerable likelihood of accessing TVWS based on the RSS status of 3D indoor active TV channels.

articleTitle: Blockchain: Tools, Challenges and Benefits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: There has been a dramatic shift in the digital world due to blockchain technology, offering decentralised, transparent, and secure solutions with applications spanning supply chains, finance, healthcare, and beyond. This paper presents an overview of blockchain technologies and tools, outlining their capabilities, benefits, and drawbacks. These include Ethereum, Hyperledger Fabric, Remix IDE, Meta Mask, Geth, Mist, IPFS, Web3.js, Corda, Dex Tools, Bitcoinj, Ganache, and Parity. It highlights the continuous endeavours to utilise blockchain to its maximum capacity by presenting the continuing attempts to overcome these obstacles via sustainability practices, standardisation initiatives, and alternative consensus mechanisms. It emphasises Collaboration among stakeholders to overcome these obstacles and achieve the digital age’s revolutionary potential of blockchain technology.

articleTitle: User Mobility Prediction in 5G Networks Using Recurrent Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The use of new possibilities introduced by 5G networks also creates new problems and concerns, specifically in the field of user mobility in wireless communication systems. In this paper, the Authors investigate the effectiveness of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) in the mobility prediction context in order to exploit the temporal component in the users movement data for improved prediction performance. To drive this process, the input datasets are obtained from the GeoLife GPS Trajectories dataset, then follow the data pre-processing steps, constructing an LSTM-based RNN model, and using Python with TensorFlow and Keras. From the analyses, we detected that the accomplishment of using LSTM and hybrid RNN-CNN is significant and higher than the traditional approaches of EN, RFM, and CL. The test results demonstrate that the LSTM model can reduce the MAE and RMSE values by 19. 49% and 14. 82%, respectively. However, the execution of these models has some issues that include compute time, instantaneous prediction that is needed in many real-world applications, and case. Such problems can be solved with the help of such approaches as edge computing and distributed processing. Besides, it is pivotal to put measures in place to maintain the confidentiality and security of user information. This paper highlights the applicative potential of RNNs in redesigning user mobility prediction in 5G networks, and thus helping toward a better ownership of the network players and assets.

articleTitle: Adaptive Modulation and Coding in 5G Networks with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: As part of the present work, it aims to examine the use of deep learning in the improvement of AMC in 5G networks. While traditional AMC methods like the ones mentioned above are applicable to previous generations of the mobile networks, they are not optimal taking into consideration the complexities and the constantly evolving nature of 5G systems. Therefore, we suggest the use of convolutional and recurrent neural networks with the aim of employing deep learning in designing an adaptive system that is capable of predicting the optimal modulation and coding schemes given instantaneous CSI information. It covers data gathering, process modeling, and implementation on a platform designed for 5G consumer network. Thus, the improvement in the data throughput rate, the level of errors, and the degree of satisfaction, obtained through the experimental results, can confirm the optimal nature of the proposed approach. It can be seen that the deep learning-based AMC system is computationally efficient and can be embedded for real-time applications, and the performance of the system is further optimised with improving learning. To conclude, this study reveals the effectiveness of deep learning in transforming AMC in 5G networks, by offering a dependable and dynamic solution the wired and wireless telecommunications networks. In a future work more towards detailing of the model and finding new architectures for the system more refined system can be achieved.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches in Optical Sensing for Precision Kidney Function Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Optical sensing presents a viable approach to non-invasive kidney function assessment, mitigating the drawbacks of invasive methods, including discomfort and cost. The study presents a unique optical sensing device that measures key kidney function parameters such as urea, glucose, creatinine, and uric acid using infrared LEDs and photodiodes. Through the utilization of these chemicals' distinct absorption spectra, the proposed system provides very accurate and precise real-time monitoring. The results show a significant improvement over current invasive procedures, with performance measures exceeding those of traditional approaches, and error margins cut in half. Regression analysis yields an R-squared value of 0.98, a Bland-Altman bias of only 0.1 mg/dL, and a Pearson's correlation coefficient of 0.95, demonstrating the proposed system's dependability and precision in clinical applications. These results from validation testing attest to the proposed system's efficacy and reliability. Overall, the study highlights how optical sensing technology can revolutionize kidney function analysis by providing a non-invasive, economical, and effective substitute for traditional techniques.

articleTitle: Cancer Genomics: Identifying Biomarkers for Early Detection and Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Genomic sciences, specifically with regards to cancer, has provided optimism in early diagnosis, treatment options by pointing to the molecular basis of cancer. This work aims at defining biomarkers for cancer diagnosis and treatment – or in other words, discovering novel biomarkers for early detection and treatment of cancer using multi-omics data from TCGA and ICGC. Ing data obtained through genome, transcriptome, and proteome studies , we revealed novel biomarkers corresponding to different types of cancer. The aforementioned datasets were processed with the help of random forests and artificial neural networks because these machine learning techniques delivered high biomarker recognition rates. This will incorporate, biomarkers such as BRCA1 for breast cancer and EGFR for lung cancer, showing high sensitivity and specificity levels. It also tackles issues such as tumor heterogeneity and presents a cardiovascular treatment plan that involves multiple disciplines. Interestingly, the assessment of genomics for cancer diagnosis and treatment has outlined such possible avenues for further investigations and practical use in the future. It is positioned in the rapidly expanding field of personalized oncology; this research seeks to improve patients’ lifestyles via the early and accurate identification of cancer.

articleTitle: FusionSegNet: Integrating Modalities for Enhanced Brain Tumor Detection and Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: Improving diagnostic accuracy and striving for thorough analysis is always crucial in medical imaging, Multi Modal Medical Imaging has proved to be a useful approach in this area, providing computational power and accuracy for tasks that humans would otherwise have a tough time doing. This paper investigates the fusion of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) with Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography (FDG-PET) or Technetium-99m-Tilmanocept Single-Photon Emission Computed Tomography (TITc-SPECT) scans which are generally used for detecting Gliomas or Metastatic Bronchogenic Carcinoma (Brain Tumors that are formed due to lung cancer). This paper targets a pipeline that will investigate the fusion of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) with Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography (FDG-PET) or Technetium-99m-Tilmanocept Single-Photon Emission Computed Tomography (TITc-SPECT) scans which are usually used to detect these brain tumors. The Denoising Diffusion image Fusion Model (DDFM) is used to combine the structural and functional information from these medical scans and the fused results of these images are then used as input to CNN as well as a U-Net model for brain tumor detection and segmentation respectively. The performance of these models is evaluated based on the probability of tumor detection and the accuracy of segmentation. The main objective of this paper is to validate the effectiveness of the DDFM fusion approach for medical scans by demonstrating tumor detection and classification accuracy in the fused multi-modal images. The results of this paper, therefore, hold a potential for improving the clinical decision-making process and making more effective strategies for brain tumor diagnosis and its management through the use of complementary imaging data.

articleTitle: Unveiling CAPTCHAs: Advanced CNN Techniques for High-Accuracy Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The development of reliable CAPTCHA systems is required because it is a persistent difficulty to differentiate between human users and artificial bots. In this study, the issue of overcoming text-based CAPTCHAs is tackled by utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), which resulted in an impressively high accuracy rate of 99%. In order to simulate the variability that exists in the actual world, the CNN model that has been developed has been rigorously trained on a wide variety of CAPTCHA images; substantial data augmentation techniques have been utilized. Through the utilization of deep learning, hence are able to improve the model's capability of recognizing and decoding complicated and deformed CAPTCHA characters. This new development highlights the significance of innovation and the implementation of cutting-edge technologies in the process of improving and strengthening cybersecurity measures. The results of the experiments verify the effectiveness of the model, exhibiting a significant improvement above conventional OCR approaches and other machine learning techniques. The deep architecture of the CNN, which is capable of capturing subtle patterns and reducing noise in CAPTCHA images, is a substantial contributor to the high level of accuracy that was attained. This research not only draws attention to the flaws that are present in the CAPTCHA systems that are now in use, but it also emphasizes the importance of developing solutions that are both more secure and inventive. With the goal of creating trust in digital platforms through the promotion of security and the reduction of fraud. It is the development of such cutting-edge technologies that contribute to the establishment of a safe digital economy, which in turn makes it possible for economic growth to be sustained over time.

articleTitle: Machine Learning and Neural Network based Early Prediction of Corona Virus and Diagnosing the Status of heart diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Computing and Signal Processing (IICCCS)
abstract: The prediction of several viruses and biomedical signal classifications in recent times have evolved tremendously with the help of machine learning models and neural networks. This paper studies coronavirus, and ECG datasets which are further trained and tested by machine learning algorithms and neural networks such as Linear Regression (LR), Logistic Regression, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest (RF) Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to predict the possibility of confirmed, cured and death cases including the symptoms related to virus attack, heart and brain disease falling under each subject post training and validation. This paper demonstrates a comparative analysis among our work and parallel research work using machine learning models and neural networks with respect to accuracy. An accuracy of (90-95)% has been achieved by machine learning algorithms during the prediction of various diseases with an error rate of approximately 6%. Furthermore, neural networks produced an accuracy of (90-92)% for the same datasets with an error rate of nearly 3%. The resultant model produces high accuracy and may be used to in embedded and IoT devices to improvise the outcome for intended diseases.
